issues.failure_explanation: If $\sigma=0$, then $\sigma\sigma^{\top}=0$, which is positive semidefinite but not positive definite. Thus all four numerical experiments lie outside the globally stated diffusion hypothesis.

issues.overall_effect: The paper's stated model framework does not cover its pure-jump numerical examples, despite pure-jump NTS dynamics being central to the experiments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\left\Vert \cdot\right\Vert $ be any given norm on $\mathbb{R}^{2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: An upper bound $\ell(z)=O(e^{-B_\ell\|z\|})$ directly makes $k<B_\ell$ a sufficient radial integrability condition, not a necessary one; the same density may decay faster and satisfy the bound for many smaller, nonunique values of $B_\ell$. Moreover, moments of exponential asset coordinates depend on directional positive tails, whereas $e^{k\|z\|}$ also penalizes harmless negative tails. Finally, the numerical threshold $B_\ell\ge2$ cannot be norm-independent when the norm is allowed to be arbitrarily rescaled.

failure_location.quote:
Since the process $X$ has finite moments of all orders up to $k\in\mathbb{N}$  if and only if  $\int_{\left\Vert z\right\Vert >\epsilon}e^{k\left\Vert z\right\Vert }\ell\left(dz\right)<\infty$ for any $\epsilon>0$, then $k<B_\ell$  provides a necessary condition of it. Following \citet[Chapter 6]{applebaum2004}, the stronger condition $B_{\ell}\geq2$ is necessary to guarantee the
existence of a unique solution with finite variance to the stochastic
differential equation (\ref{eq: intro - asset prices dynamics}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted equivalence and necessity by correctly normalized sufficient conditions, or formulate and justify directional exponential-moment hypotheses tailored to the coefficients $e^{z^{(i)}}-1$.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's justification of its moment and well-posedness assumptions is false as written, and the claimed necessity of the radial $B_\ell$ threshold is unsupported.
issues.title: Tail decay is incorrectly characterized as a necessary moment condition
issues.why_classification: The repair requires more than changing a symbol: the radial moment characterization and norm-dependent threshold must be reformulated, though this can be done without changing the numerical architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Here, to account for the non-smoothness of

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm fixes $\theta=1/2$ and executes the ordinary full-step loop starting at $n=1$. It never replaces the first step by four backward-Euler quarter-steps. Those steps also require quarter-step characteristic grids, interpolation matrices, and a different system matrix or factorization, none of which are included in the precomputations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a separate four-quarter-step $\theta=1$ startup stage, including the corresponding departure grid, interpolation operator, system matrix, preconditioner, and fixed-point solves, before continuing with the $\theta=1/2$ full-step loop.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg: template of the algorithm is not the complete procedure described in the text and does not implement the damping used to address the nonsmooth payoff; consequently, its claimed relation to the reported second-order computations is unreliable.
issues.title: The stated complete algorithm omits the required damping steps
issues.why_classification: The method can be preserved, but repairing the executable algorithm requires a distinct startup branch and additional operators and solves rather than a purely local textual correction.
